description: Get full details for one TV show by TMDB id: overview, genres, keywords (`{id, name}`), seasons/episodes counts, networks, created_by (the show's creator(s)), status, the age/content rating (certification) for `region` (falling back to the US rating, then any available country, when `region` has none; check `certification_region` to see which one was used), and links. By default also includes IMDb/Rotten Tomatoes/Metacritic ratings and an awards summary (see include_ratings), plus OMDb's own age rating (`ratings.rated`, separate from this tool's `certification`; the two can differ), from OMDb (set include_ratings=false to skip). If unavailable (no OMDB_API_KEY, no imdb_id, or the OMDb lookup fails), `ratings` degrades to `{found:false, reason}` instead of failing the call. For shows like this one, get_tv_recommendations is the first stop; to match its themes instead, pass 2-3 distinctive keyword ids to discover_tv's with_keywords. A show's keywords are sparser, so ',' (all) often matches only the show itself and '|' (any) is the usual pick (checked live: Breaking Bad's 'drug dealer'|'outlaw' give The Sopranos, Narcos, Peaky Blinders). Set expand_episodes=true to also pull the seasons' episode lists (up to 250 episodes, 50 per season; see that field) instead of calling get_tv_season per season. If you only need the headline info (name/year/genres/vote average, season/episode counts), for one id or several, use get_tv_shows: it's trimmed and skips the rest of this payload. Get the id from search_tv.

expand_episodes.description: Also fetch every season's full episode list (name, air date, runtime, and TMDB `vote_average`, TMDB's own 0-10 user score, not this tool's IMDb/RT/Metacritic `ratings`) as `seasons_detail`, in one extra request (more only past 20 seasons). Use this instead of calling get_tv_season once per season when you need all episodes of a multi-season show. Episode overviews are omitted to keep the response usable; call get_tv_season for one season's full detail including overview. Each season's episode list is capped at 50 (season 0 'Specials' can otherwise run to hundreds of bonus clips), the combined count across every season is capped at 250, and the whole aggregate has a hard size ceiling (it trims further if episode names are unusually long), since a 30+ season show could otherwise still exceed a usable size. `episode_count` on each season still reports that season's true total. The 250 budget is spent in season order starting at season 0, so on a long-running show the specials are served first and the last seasons fall off. A season entirely beyond the 250-episode budget is skipped rather than fetched and discarded, so its `overview`/`poster_url` come back null too, not just its `episodes` list; call get_tv_season for that season's full detail.

include_ratings.description: Add IMDb/Rotten Tomatoes/Metacritic ratings and an awards summary from OMDb (requires OMDB_API_KEY). The summary is free text (major-award wins/nominations: Oscars, Emmys, Golden Globes, etc., whatever OMDb aggregates), not a structured count, and covers the whole film/show, not any one person's award. Set false to skip the extra lookup.

language.description: Response language (ISO-639-1, optionally with a region), e.g. 'ru-RU' or 'en-US'; pass the user's language when it isn't the default. Localizes titles/overviews/genre names. A well-formed code TMDB has no translation for (e.g. 'xx') is not an error: overviews come back null, movies/shows keep their original-language title, and episodes get a generic 'Episode N' name.

region.description: The user's country (pass it when known), whose age rating `certification` shows (falling back to the US rating, then any country's).

name: get_tv

imdb_rating.description: IMDb user score, 0-10, as a string, e.g. '6.5'. Not TMDB's `vote_average`.

metascore.description: Metacritic critic score, 0-100 scale, as a string, e.g. '67'.

rotten_tomatoes.description: Rotten Tomatoes Tomatometer — the percentage of positive critic reviews, as a string including the sign, e.g. '79%'. Not a 0-10 or 0-100 score.

vote_average.description: TMDB's own 0-10 user score. A different audience and scale from the IMDb/RT/Metacritic scores get_movie/get_tv return as `ratings` — don't compare, average or substitute across the two.
